basics.name: Abdur Rehman Khan
basics.label: Computer Science Student · Agentic Software Development
basics.headline: I build real products with AI agents, organised like a small engineering team.
basics.summary: Computer Science student in Karachi who builds software with AI agents: agent sub-agents, skills and hooks, a second coding agent, user stories, gated delivery pipelines, and full-stack TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js and PostgreSQL.

highlights.label: Unsak, an offline-first app for students
Gated steps from user story to merged code

paragraphs: I started in cybersecurity, with lab work and CTFs, and moved toward building software. Most of my work now is agentic development: AI coding agents with clear roles, files they own, written task briefs, and checks they must pass before anything merges.
I have used this setup on a NASA Space Apps hackathon game, a live student well-being app and this portfolio.
strengths: Multi-agent setups with coding agents (sub-agents, skills, hooks)
Spec-driven delivery: user stories, sprints, gates and a Definition of Done
Full-stack web development with TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js and PostgreSQL
A security mindset from lab work, CTFs and OWASP reviews

process.title: Specify
process.description: Product spec, requirements and user stories with IDs. Every decision goes in a log.

process.title: Plan
process.description: The tech-lead agent splits a story into parts, each with an owner and a list of files.

process.title: Build
process.description: builder agent and other builder agents work from written briefs, only in the files they own.

process.title: Review
process.description: lead agent reviews every diff. Rejected work goes back with a written fix brief.

process.title: Test & audit
process.description: Tests, accessibility, device and OWASP security checks run as blocking gates.

process.title: Merge
process.description: Only after the QA gate passes. Sensitive changes wait for my sign-off.

projects.title: Moon Base Cadets
projects.summary: A browser game for children aged 7–12. Players run a Moon or Mars base for 10 days while real solar flares and storms from NASA's DONKI records hit it.
projects.role: Product owner and game designer in a three-person team. the coding agent was tech lead and frontend engineer; builder agent was backend engineer.
points: Written file ownership per agent, task briefs and result files for every backend job
Four time-boxed gates across the hackathon weekend, tracked on a task board
Every science fact links to a NASA source; game rules are labelled as game rules
No accounts, cookies or tracking, because the players are children

projects.title: Unsak Digital Companion
projects.summary: A mobile-first app that helps students build better phone habits: a 30-day challenge, a bedtime wind-down, a scam-message check and people to talk to.
projects.role: Started as a Design Thinking course project with user interviews and journey maps. lead agent wrote the module contract and builder agent built the modules in parallel.
points: Sign-in with Google or a 6-digit email code
Personal data stays on the device, with export in Settings
Works offline and installs to the home screen
